def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data.physical_scope: Conditional data definition for electric and magnetic charge labels, second-helicity BPS indices, and marginal-stability chambers in an already specified pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) quantum or regulated one-particle model on regular Seiberg–Witten patches; it asserts no state existence, continuum QFT construction, or physical realization of Hall counts.

def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data:
## Definition

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Let $U$ be a simply connected regular patch of its source-proposed Seiberg–Witten Coulomb branch on which the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. The earlier Coulomb-branch data define the formal charge-label lattice $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with labels $\gamma=(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The source-proposed model convention fixes the scalar central charge to be $z_u(\gamma)=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)$; $a,a_D,z_u$ have mass dimension one, $u$ has mass dimension two, and charge labels and pairings are dimensionless.

For the model-specific physical charge data used here, equip $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ with the integral antisymmetric Dirac pairing

$$\langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_m n'_e-n_e n'_m).$$

In particular the source-designated monopole label $\gamma_m=(0,1)$ and dyon label $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$ satisfy $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$, the convention matched by a two-arrow Kronecker quiver with both arrows directed from the dyon vertex to the monopole vertex. The lattice records formal charge labels only: it does not assert that every label is an allowed line operator or a realized particle.

For each $u\in U$, the selected model supplies a stable support $\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$, supply a one-particle massive rest-fiber Hilbert sector $\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ carrying the selected unitary four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ super-Poincaré representation at rest momentum $P^\mu=(M_{u,\gamma},0,0,0)$ in metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with conserved charge $\gamma$, positive scalar rest mass $M_{u,\gamma}$, and scalar central-charge block $Z^{12}=z_u(\gamma)$, $Z^{21}=-z_u(\gamma)$. Supply a nonzero closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ invariant under the chosen massive little-group rotations and identified as the selected BPS sector. Its vectors lie in the common supercharge domain, and every nonzero vector is BPS-saturated in the exact sense of the earlier BPS-state definition: $M_{u,\gamma}=|z_u(\gamma)|$, and the two N=2 annihilating supercharge combinations in that definition vanish on them. Stability is supplied model data: this sector is discrete and separated by a positive spectral gap from the multiparticle continuum at the same conserved charge. The sector and gap are inputs, not conclusions here. On this sector let $J_3$ be the self-adjoint generator of rotations about a fixed spatial axis in the restricted unitary representation of the massive little group, normalized so that $2J_3$ has integer spectrum. Require its spectral calculus to define a bounded trace-class operator $B_{u,\gamma}=(-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2$, and supply a Hilbert basis $E_{u,\gamma}$ of $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$.

Define the four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ second-helicity supertrace, also called the $B_2$ index here, by

$$\Omega_u(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}(B_{u,\gamma}),$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}$ is the absolutely convergent supplied-basis trace of a trace-class operator; basis independence is not needed here. Set $\Omega_u(\gamma)=0$ for $\gamma\notin\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$. The trace convention uses only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the stated mathematical suppliers, not full Choice. No existence or local constancy of this support is asserted.

For a chosen locally finite set of nonzero charges whose central charges lie, after one fixed rotation by a real phase $\alpha$, in the open upper half-plane, define $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi\in(0,1)$. For two charges with nonzero central charges, their marginal-stability wall is the locus in $U$ where $z_u(\gamma)/z_u(\delta)\in\mathbb R_{>0}$; a chamber is a connected component of the regular patch after removing the specified wall loci. A formal positive cone $\Gamma_+\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ used for ordered products contains $0$, is closed under addition, and is pointed ($\Gamma_+\cap(-\Gamma_+)=\{0\}$). It is supplied with an additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ that is positive on nonzero charges and has finite sublevel sets, meaning $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\in\mathbb N$. The definition is conditional on the existence of the Hilbert sectors, trace data, cone, and degree; it constructs no continuum theory and makes no Hall-index identification.

pthm-qftx-physical-bps-wall-crossing.physical_scope: Conditional wall-crossing identity for the second-helicity BPS index of an already specified pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) model on regular Coulomb-branch chambers, provided a locally finite finite-quiver presentation and an exact coefficient-, charge-, pairing-, and factor-preserving Hall-to-Hilbert bridge are supplied; it asserts neither that this bridge exists nor a continuum QFT construction.

pthm-qftx-physical-bps-wall-crossing:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the supplied trace-class BPS-index data. Use the physical charge datum on a regular pure-SU(2) Seiberg–Witten patch and let $u_-$ and $u_+$ be points in two chambers. Write $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ for its second-helicity supertrace and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}$ for its integral antisymmetric pairing. The finite-field Hall input is a finite acyclic quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb F_q$, where $q>1$ is a prime power, with the subobject-first, total-dimension-completed skew Hall generator from the mathematical supplier. Let

$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d),\qquad t=\sqrt q>0.$$

Suppose an additive map $\rho:\mathbb Z^{Q_0}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and a physical charge cone $\Gamma_+$ are supplied, where $\Gamma_+$ contains $0$, is closed under addition and is pointed, such that $\rho(\mathbb N^{Q_0})\subseteq\Gamma_+$. Supply a positive additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with finite sublevel sets and $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$, and assume

$$\langle\rho(\mathbf d),\rho(\mathbf e)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q.$$

Choose one real phase rotation $\alpha$ such that for both $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ the vertex charges $Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf e_i))$ lie in the upper half-plane, with the decreasing Hall phase order matching the chosen physical BPS-ray order. Assume the nonzero BPS-index support lies in $\Gamma_+$, is locally finite in the $\ell$-completion, and has $\Omega_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb Z$ on its support.

Let $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ be a coefficient field containing a fixed $\hbar$ and a field embedding $\sigma:\mathbb Q(t)\to K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ with $\sigma(t)=\hbar$. Define the completed physical charge torus with basis $Y^\gamma$ and multiplication

$$Y^\gamma\star_\hbar Y^\delta=\hbar^{-\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\gamma+\delta}.$$

The charge map and coefficient embedding define the degree-continuous torus map $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})=Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}$, $\Phi(c x^{\mathbf d})=\sigma(c)Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}$. On the commutative completed charge series with basis $y^\delta$ for $\delta\in\Gamma_+$, supply a sign refinement $\varepsilon:\Gamma_+\to\{\pm1\}$ with $\varepsilon(0)=1$ and $\varepsilon(\gamma+\delta)=(-1)^{\langle\gamma,\delta\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}\varepsilon(\gamma)\varepsilon(\delta)$. Define the physical KS factor at supported charge $\gamma$ by

$$\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}(y^\delta)=y^\delta\bigl(1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma\bigr)^{\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}.$$

The integer power is interpreted by its formal binomial series in the pointed degree completion. Let $\mathcal S_u$ be the composition of these factors over the stable BPS support in decreasing phase order, with the largest phase leftmost. Finally assume an exact model-specific bridge: there is a continuous group homomorphism $\Theta$ from units of the physical completed quantum torus to continuous automorphisms of the commutative charge series, and for every phase $\phi$ and either chamber it satisfies

$$\Theta\!\left(\Phi(J(S_{Z_u}(\phi)))\right)=\prod_{\substack{\gamma\in\Gamma_+\\\phi_u(\gamma)=\phi}}^{\searrow}\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}.$$

Here $S_{Z_u}(\phi)$ and $J$ are the semistable phase factor and skew integration from the finite-field Hall definition. Then

$$\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}.$$

This is a conditional transport theorem. The specified per-phase bridge is an additional physical input; neither the finite-field Hall identity nor this theorem asserts that the pure-SU(2) model supplies it, that the resulting index counts exist, or that the model has a continuum quantum-field-theory construction.

ex-qftx-physical-bps-kronecker-hall-sect.physical_scope: A conditional pure-SU(2) monopole/dyon charge example whose local proof counts finite-field representations and their Hall groupoid weight; the finite-field coefficient is not identified with a physical second-helicity index, and no BPS state or continuum QFT is asserted to exist.
